title: AI subscriptions as governed workers
subtitle: Running vendors' authenticated command-line tools as governed workers, alongside API-keyed and local models

stats.label: metered usage entries, each tied to the work that spent it
overall cache hit rate across one priced engineering program

lede: My governance platform runs real interactive sessions of vendors' authenticated command-line tools, under my own logins, as durable governed seats, alongside API-keyed seats and local open-source models served on my own GPUs. Every seat is metered against the work that used it, and cheap is the default: a role contract names its model and reasoning effort as data, so the lead, planning and architecture seats use a heavier model than the development seats on purpose. Start with Directing AI coding agents at program scale and What the work cost, to the penny.
quote: Builders and reviewers come from different model families so their blind spots do not overlap.
evidence: Agent orchestration across vendors: vendors' authenticated command-line tools run as durable governed seats beside API-keyed and local open-weight seats, under the same acceptance rules.
Cost attribution for AI work: 31,811 metered usage records tied to the work that spent them, and one program costed by phase with a 94.5% overall cache hit rate.
Separation of duties for AI work: builders and reviewers drawn from different model families so their blind spots do not overlap.
Prompt delivery assurance: a prompt counts as delivered only when the provider's own transcript shows it, within a 30 s acceptance deadline.
author: Corey James
